The 27-year-old Cebuana, who won bronze in the women’s -63kg division last year, will compete in the lower weight class at -61kg. Also seeing action are 2026 Asian Games bronze medalist and reigning Asian Junior champion Albert Ian Delos Santos (men’s 70kg), Rose Jean Ramos (women’s 49kg), Rosegie Ramos (women’s 53kg), and Kristel Macrohon (women’s 69kg). According to the International Weightlifting Federation, athletes must compete in a minimum of five of the 10 qualifying competitions to earn a ranking for the 2028 Olympics. The calendar is split into two periods, with Period One consisting of six events and three totals needed, and Period Two consisting of four events and two totals needed. This tournament opens the Period One, which will end in the 2027 world championships in September. Period Two events will run from November 2027 until May 2028.

headline: Russian Tourists Skip Crowded Sochi for Fiji and Madagascar as Prices Parity Hits
snippet: On the coastal highway between Juba and Sochi, traffic has ground to a halt, a familiar sight for domestic tourists during peak season. Yet, in an airport lounge in Moscow, a family is comparing the cost of a week in the Caucasus with a package to the Indian Ocean islands. The math, they find, no longer favors the domestic resort. This shift marks a tangible break in the Russian tourism market: a segment of budget-conscious travelers is bypassing crowded southern regions in favor of long-haul destinations like Fiji and Madagascar, driven by a convergence of rising local prices and competitive international airfares. According to data from the telecommunications company MegaFon, this is not a fleeting trend but a structural change in booking behavior. While domestic tourist traffic grew by a modest 4.3%, demand for remote international destinations surged. Fiji recorded a 147% increase in subscribers, while Madagascar saw Russian tourist numbers rise by 2.6 times. Cabo Verde and Jamaica also posted significant growth of 79% and 61%, respectively. This data suggests a reallocation of spending rather than a simple increase in travel volume. The Price Parity Point The driving force behind this shift is economic. For a family, a one-week holiday in a quality hotel in Sirius or Krasnaya Polyana now costs between 250,000 and 300,000 rubles, inclusive of flights, transfers, and on-site expenses. This price point has become comparable to package tours to Africa or Oceania. Ilya Rodenko, a tourism market analyst, told Pravda. Ru that the middle class is increasingly reluctant to overpay for overloaded infrastructure in southern Russia. When travelers compare the final bill for a domestic trip with the cost of an exotic island getaway, they often find that the latter offers a higher quality of rest and more unique experiences for a similar investment.

Archbishop scrambles to wash his hands of Trump after laying them on him: report
snippet: The Denver archbishop who led a prayer over President Donald Trump in the Oval Office is now scrambling to explain himself. Archbishop James Golka told the Denver Catholic, the archdiocese's own newspaper, on Friday that the White House's video of the Oct. 22 prayer was never meant as an endorsement, even as he defended being there and turned his fire on critics. "I understand that many people saw the video, posted by the Administration twelve days before an election, as an endorsement," Golka said. "That was never my intention." The invitation came months ago, according to the archbishop, following a June session in which faith leaders pressed the administration on immigration, religious freedom and visas for religious workers. He said progress made by task forces after that meeting encouraged him to accept, even though he knew the meeting "could be shared and some might use it for political purposes." Golka said he learned only shortly before the visit that he would be the one praying over Trump. The bishops first spent three hours with the White House Faith Office discussing religious worker visas, protection of life, religious freedom and school choice. "I've had a lot of people, really good friends, ask me, 'What were you doing?' 'Why did you do that?' I just answer, 'I was being a Catholic priest,'" he said. The archbishop then pointed outward. "I'm heartbroken that people are hurt, and that there are people intentionally using this moment to sow disunity. That's not a fruit of the Spirit," he said, urging Catholics to look past headlines he described as "often crafted to provoke." The fallout has reached Rome. Catholic commentator Christopher Hale reported in his Letters from Leo newsletter that a senior official at the Vatican's Dicastery for Bishops called it "a highly inappropriate meeting and insult to Pope Leo." Hale wrote that Golka's account stops short of an apology and never mentions Paula White-Cain, the televangelist and White House Faith Office adviser who stood behind Trump's chair as the bishops laid hands on him. The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops has said it neither organized the meeting nor has any affiliation with it. Golka closed with a pledge. "This work helps only if the Church carries the same message to leaders of both parties. We will," he said.

headline: Dubai Police launch pedestrian safety campaign, warn of AED 400 fine for unsafe crossing
snippet: Dubai: Dubai Police have launched an awareness campaign across police station jurisdictions in the emirate to promote pedestrian safety, encourage responsible road behaviour and reduce traffic accidents. Organised by the General Department of Police Stations in cooperation with the General Department of Traffic, the campaign focuses on educating pedestrians and motorists about traffic regulations, designated crossing points and the importance of following traffic signals. Brigadier Majid Sultan Al Suwaidi, Director of the General Department of Police Stations, said the initiative forms part of Dubai Police’s ongoing efforts to strengthen road safety awareness and encourage responsible behaviour among all road users. He stressed that using designated pedestrian crossings, following traffic signals and remaining alert while crossing roads are essential to preventing accidents and protecting lives. Officers take awareness campaign to the streets Brig Al Suwaidi explained that officers and personnel from police stations across Dubai have been conducting field visits within their respective jurisdictions to provide pedestrians with practical guidance on safe road crossing. The campaign also targets motorists, reminding them to remain vigilant, reduce speed and give way to pedestrians at designated crossings, particularly in busy and densely populated areas. “Road safety is a shared responsibility. Everyone has a role to play in following traffic regulations and helping create safer roads for all,” he emphasised. AED 400 fine for unsafe crossing Brig Al Suwaidi urged pedestrians to use designated crossings, check that the road is clear of approaching vehicles and obey pedestrian traffic signals at intersections. He also reminded motorists to remain attentive to pedestrian movement and maintain safe speeds, especially in areas with heavy foot traffic. He highlighted that Article 89 of the Federal Traffic Law stipulates an AED 400 fine for pedestrians who disregard traffic signals or cross roads at undesignated locations. Brig Al Suwaidi concluded by encouraging residents and visitors to cooperate with the relevant authorities and follow road safety instructions, reaffirming Dubai Police’s commitment to reducing traffic accidents and protecting all road users.
